project.idea_text: An online food delivery app where customers order from nearby restaurants, pay online and follow the courier live, while restaurants run their menus and orders and couriers deliver.

summary: An online food delivery platform for one city: customers browse, order, pay and track, restaurants run menus and orders, and couriers deliver. 13 requirements become 4 epics, 10 stories and 27 tasks (117 points) over 4 sprints.
assumptions: Single-city launch with about 200 restaurants and 50 couriers.
Card and wallet payments go through a hosted payment provider; the platform never stores card numbers.
Couriers use a mobile web app in v1; there are no native iOS or Android apps.
Restaurants are onboarded by operations staff; there is no self-service restaurant sign-up in v1.
Delivery fees are flat per restaurant; promotions, coupons and surge pricing are out of scope.
The team is four full-stack developers working in 10-day sprints.

requirements.text: Customers can find restaurants near their location and browse menus, filtering by cuisine and searching by name or dish.
Customers can add dishes to a cart and place an order for a chosen delivery address, with optional notes for the restaurant.
Customers, restaurant staff and couriers can register and sign in; customers keep saved addresses and their order history.
Customers can pay online by card or digital wallet; an order reaches the restaurant only after the payment is confirmed.
Customers can follow an order from accepted to delivered and see the courier's position on a map while it is on the way.
Customers receive a push, SMS or email notification when the order status changes.
Restaurant staff can edit menu items, prices and availability, and changes appear to customers within one minute.
Restaurant staff see new orders as they arrive and can accept or reject each one, stating a preparation time.
Couriers receive delivery offers, accept one, and update its status from pickup to hand-over.
Customers can rate the restaurant and the courier after delivery and leave a short review.
Restaurant search and menu pages respond in under 2 seconds at the 95th percentile on a 4G connection, with 5,000 restaurants in the catalogue.
Card data never reaches the platform's servers; passwords are stored only as salted hashes; all traffic uses HTTPS.
Ordering is available 99.5% of each month, and an accepted order is never lost when a service restarts.

epics.title: Customer Ordering
epics.description: Everything a customer does before paying: finding a restaurant, building a cart, placing an order and keeping an account.

epics.title: Payments and Live Tracking
epics.description: Taking the payment securely, moving the order through its states and keeping the customer informed until delivery.

epics.title: Restaurant and Courier Operations
epics.description: The tools restaurant staff and couriers use to run their side of an order.

epics.title: Platform and Reliability
epics.description: Build pipeline, monitoring, performance and end-to-end verification so the service can launch and stay up.

stories.i_want: to search and browse nearby restaurants by cuisine, name or dish
stories.so_that: I can quickly find something I want to eat
acceptance_criteria: The restaurant list shows only restaurants that deliver to the customer's location, sorted by distance by default.
Customers can filter by cuisine and search by restaurant or dish name.
A menu shows each item with a photo, price and description; unavailable items are greyed out and cannot be added.
Search and menu pages respond in under 2 seconds at the 95th percentile.

stories.i_want: to add dishes to a cart and place an order for my delivery address
stories.so_that: the food is prepared and brought to my door
acceptance_criteria: A cart holds items from one restaurant only; adding an item from another restaurant asks the customer to start a new cart.
The cart shows item totals, the delivery fee and the order total, and updates them as quantities change.
Checkout requires a delivery address and accepts an optional note to the restaurant.
If an item becomes unavailable or its price changes, the customer is told before the order is placed.

stories.i_want: to register and sign in with my email and password
stories.so_that: my addresses and order history are saved
acceptance_criteria: A user can register with an email address and a password of at least 10 characters.
Passwords are stored only as salted hashes and sessions expire after 30 days of inactivity.
Signed-in customers can save, edit and delete delivery addresses and view past orders.
Restaurant staff and couriers sign in through the same service and only see their own tools.

stories.i_want: to pay for my order by card or digital wallet
stories.so_that: my order is confirmed without handling cash
acceptance_criteria: Card details are entered in the payment provider's hosted fields and never reach our servers.
An order is sent to the restaurant only after the provider confirms the payment.
A declined payment shows a clear message and keeps the cart so the customer can retry.
A payment confirmation is shown on screen and sent by email, and duplicate webhooks never charge or confirm twice.

stories.i_want: to watch my order progress and see the courier on a map
stories.so_that: I know when to expect my food
acceptance_criteria: The order page shows the current status: placed, accepted, preparing, picked up, delivered or cancelled.
While the order is on the way, the courier's position on the map refreshes at least every 10 seconds.
The page updates without a manual refresh and recovers after a dropped connection.
An accepted order and its status history are stored durably and survive a service restart.

stories.i_want: to be notified when my order changes status
stories.so_that: I do not have to keep the app open
acceptance_criteria: A notification is sent when the order is accepted, picked up and delivered.
Customers can choose push, SMS or email, and can switch notifications off.
A failed notification is retried and never blocks the order from moving forward.

stories.i_want: to edit my menu, prices and item availability
stories.so_that: customers always see what I can really serve
acceptance_criteria: A manager can add, edit and delete menu items with name, description, photo and price.
An item can be switched to unavailable with one action and is immediately greyed out for customers.
Menu changes are visible to customers within one minute.
Only staff of that restaurant can change its menu.

stories.i_want: to see new orders and accept or reject them with a preparation time
stories.so_that: I stay in control of the kitchen's workload
acceptance_criteria: A new paid order appears in the inbox within 5 seconds and plays a sound until it is answered.
Staff can accept an order with a preparation time, or reject it with a reason.
An order that is not answered within 3 minutes is cancelled and the customer is refunded.

stories.i_want: to receive delivery offers, accept one and update its status
stories.so_that: I can pick up and deliver orders efficiently
acceptance_criteria: When an order is accepted, nearby available couriers receive an offer showing pickup, drop-off and earnings.
The first courier to accept gets the job; the others see it disappear.
The courier marks the order picked up and delivered, and the app shares the courier's position while the job is active.
If no courier accepts within 5 minutes, operations staff are alerted.

stories.i_want: automated deployment, monitoring and load testing
stories.so_that: ordering stays fast and available as traffic grows
acceptance_criteria: Every merge to the main branch is built, tested and deployed to a staging environment automatically.
Error rate, latency and queue depth are visible on a dashboard, and an alert fires when ordering fails for 5 minutes.
A load test of search and checkout confirms the 2-second p95 target before release.
An end-to-end test covers the full order journey from sign-in to delivery.

tasks.title: Wireframes and design system for the ordering flow
tasks.description: Wireframes for search, menu, cart, checkout and tracking, plus a small component library (buttons, cards, form fields) shared by all web screens.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Five screens at low fidelity and one shared component set; no user research.

tasks.title: Restaurant and menu database schema
tasks.description: Tables for restaurants, delivery zones, menus, menu items and availability, with a geospatial index for nearby search.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Standard relational model; the geo index and delivery zones add the uncertainty.

tasks.title: Restaurant search and menu API
tasks.description: Endpoints to list restaurants near a point, filter by cuisine, full-text search on restaurant and dish names, and return a menu. Paginated and cached.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Geo query plus text search plus caching to meet the 2-second target.

tasks.title: Restaurant list and menu screens
tasks.description: Responsive list with filters and search box, and a menu page with item cards and greyed-out unavailable items.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Two screens with filters, loading and empty states.

tasks.title: Order and order-item schema
tasks.description: Orders, order items with price snapshots, delivery address, status history and a payment reference.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Price snapshots and status history add two tables beyond the basics.

tasks.title: Cart and order placement API
tasks.description: Cart endpoints with single-restaurant validation, price and availability re-check at checkout, fee calculation and order creation in the pending-payment state.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Several validation rules and a transactional order write.

tasks.title: Cart and checkout screens
tasks.description: Cart drawer, quantity editing, address picker with saved addresses, note field and order summary.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Stateful cart UI with address handling and error states.

tasks.title: User, role and address schema
tasks.description: Users with roles (customer, restaurant staff, courier, operations), credentials and saved addresses.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Three small tables with no unusual constraints.

tasks.title: Authentication and session API
tasks.description: Register, sign in and sign out with salted password hashing, session expiry, role checks and rate limiting on sign-in.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Security-sensitive, so extra care and review time.

tasks.title: Sign-up, sign-in and address book screens
tasks.description: Registration and sign-in forms with validation, plus saved-address management and order history list.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Standard forms and one list screen.

tasks.title: Integrate payment provider (hosted fields and webhooks)
tasks.description: Set up the provider account and test mode, create payment intents, verify webhook signatures, handle retries and idempotency keys.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Third-party API with webhooks, idempotency and sandbox onboarding; the largest unknown in the plan.

tasks.title: Payment and order confirmation flow
tasks.description: Attach a payment intent to a pending order, move the order to paid on a confirmed webhook, handle declines, and refund on cancellation.
tasks.estimate_rationale: State transitions and failure paths around money.

tasks.title: Payment form and confirmation screen
tasks.description: Embed the provider's hosted card fields in checkout, show decline messages and the confirmation page.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Small UI around an embedded component.

tasks.title: Order status state machine and live update stream
tasks.description: Allowed transitions from placed to delivered or cancelled, an audit trail, and a server-sent event stream the customer page subscribes to.
tasks.estimate_rationale: State machine plus a streaming endpoint that must survive reconnects.

tasks.title: Map tiles and courier location ingestion
tasks.description: Choose a map SDK, accept courier position updates and expose the latest position per active order.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Vendor SDK plus a small write-heavy endpoint.

tasks.title: Live order tracking page with map
tasks.description: Status timeline, estimated arrival, and a map with the courier marker updating from the event stream.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Map rendering and live updates with reconnect handling.

tasks.title: Notification gateway for push, SMS and email
tasks.description: Connect push, SMS and email providers behind one interface, with templates, user preferences and retry on failure.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Three providers behind one interface; templates are short.

tasks.title: Restaurant menu management API
tasks.description: Create, update and delete items, toggle availability, and enforce that staff can only touch their own restaurant.
tasks.estimate_rationale: CRUD with an ownership check and cache invalidation.

tasks.title: Restaurant dashboard: menu editor
tasks.description: Menu editor with image upload, price editing and a one-tap availability switch.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Form-heavy screen with image upload.

tasks.title: Restaurant order inbox with accept and reject
tasks.description: Live inbox with an audible alert, accept with preparation time, reject with reason, and the 3-minute timeout countdown.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Real-time list with sound and a countdown.

tasks.title: Courier matching and dispatch service
tasks.description: Find available couriers near the restaurant, send offers, award the job to the first acceptance, and escalate when nobody accepts.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Concurrency on the first-accept rule plus timeouts and escalation.

tasks.title: Courier web app: offers, jobs and status updates
tasks.description: Mobile web app showing offers, the active job, pickup and drop-off actions, and sending the courier's position.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Mobile-first with geolocation permissions and background updates.

tasks.title: CI/CD pipeline and staging environment
tasks.description: Build and test on every merge, deploy to staging, and manage secrets and database migrations.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Pipeline, environment and migrations from scratch.

tasks.title: Monitoring, logging and alerting
tasks.description: Structured logs, a metrics dashboard for errors, latency and queue depth, and alert rules for failed ordering.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Hosted tooling with a handful of dashboards and alerts.

tasks.title: End-to-end order journey tests
tasks.description: Automated browser tests from sign-in through payment (test mode), restaurant acceptance, courier delivery and customer tracking.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Multi-actor scenario across three web apps.

tasks.title: Load test of search and checkout
tasks.description: Scripted load against search and checkout with 5,000 restaurants of seed data, reporting the p95 latency.
tasks.estimate_rationale: One tool, two scenarios and a seed script.

tasks.title: Production release and rollback runbook
tasks.description: Promote the release to production, verify with a smoke test and document the rollback steps.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Mostly checklist work once the pipeline exists.

risks.title: The backend chain decides the finish date
risks.description: CPM duration is 172 h (28.5 working days); 9 of 27 tasks (33%) are critical. Layer backend holds 112 of 172 critical-path hours (65%). Most of the longest path is backend work done one task after another, so a slip in any of those tasks moves the release date, and a second developer cannot shorten a chain of dependent tasks.
risks.mitigation: Name an owner per critical backend task, review designs before coding starts, and split the largest tasks so that frontend and testing work can begin on agreed API contracts while the backend is built.

risks.title: Payment and order state work gates tracking, notifications and couriers
risks.description: T-012 "Payment and order confirmation flow" has 9 downstream tasks and 0 h slack (CPM). T-014 "Order status state machine and live update stream" has 7 downstream tasks and 0 h slack (CPM). Both tasks sit on the critical path, and the payment provider's sandbox onboarding and webhook behaviour are outside the team's control.
risks.mitigation: Open the payment provider account and start its sandbox integration in the first sprint, agree the order status transitions early so dependent screens can use a stub, and keep a mock payment mode for demos.

risks.title: The sprints have no spare capacity
risks.description: 1 of 4 sprints is packed to at least 98% of capacity, so there is no buffer for estimation error. A plan that is already full cannot absorb sick days, review rework or one underestimated task.
risks.mitigation: Move low-priority work out of the first two sprints, leave a deliberate buffer in sprint planning, and re-estimate after the first sprint using the real completed points.

risks.title: Little testing before a late integration point
risks.description: Testing is 8 of 117 points (6.8%), below the 10% minimum. T-025 "End-to-end order journey tests" has 5 direct predecessors (integration bottleneck). Problems between the customer, restaurant and courier screens would first show up near the end, when little time is left to fix them.
risks.mitigation: Add unit and API tests to each backend task definition of done, add a payment-flow test task, and run a thin end-to-end journey as soon as checkout works rather than waiting for the last screen.

risks.title: High-severity signal: critical_high_fanout
risks.description: T-002 "Restaurant and menu database schema" has 18 downstream tasks and 0 h slack (CPM).
risks.mitigation: Review this signal with the team, assign an owner and decide whether the task can be split or started earlier.
